topic: school-specific (Vanderbilt): stats, ED rounds, supplemental fit
speaker_role: former assistant director of undergraduate admissions (Duke) plus a colleague who is a Vanderbilt alum and former Vanderbilt admissions staffer
commercial_incentive: Yes: IvyWise is a paid counseling firm and the video mentions its mock-committee process for clients.
key_insights: Vanderbilt is test optional through at least the 2026-27 cycle, with very high scores among enrolled students.
Speaker sees no stated preference between ED rounds but notes a statistical advantage to applying early, with ED2 possibly more selective than ED1.
Vanderbilt's required Immersion program favors applicants who have started their own projects or taken initiative outside class.
The 'dare to grow' theme in the supplement suggests writing a personal narrative on stepping out of your comfort zone, tied to identity or background and to what you'd add to campus.
Treat the essay as a personal story rather than a five-paragraph school essay.
Vanderbilt no longer offers interviews but allows an optional 60 to 90 second video.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Class of 2029: over 50,000 applications, about 2,300 admitted, 4.6% overall acceptance (speaker).
Enrolled class of 2028 middle 50%: SAT 1510-1560, ACT 34-35 (speaker).
notable_or_distinctive: Compact, current Vanderbilt data and the link between Immersion Vanderbilt and the supplement prompt.
reliability_notes: Short promotional video from a counseling firm; speaker says 'at least through 2026-27' for testing and the ED2 claim is unsupported by data.
